Early pilots at the central branch handled about 120 visitors per week, and the most common request was help writing job applications. Library director Meera Nair said the goal is to give residents who cannot afford private tutoring access to the same tools that wealthier students already use. Critics have asked how the library will prevent staff from seeing sensitive personal documents, and Nair replied that all sessions follow a no-storage rule: nothing typed during a session is saved, and staff are trained to warn visitors before they paste personal information. The network will publish a public report after the first six months covering usage numbers and any privacy incidents.

A two-year cloud seeding trial conducted over three districts has produced a measured rainfall increase of between four and seven percent compared with unseeded control areas, researchers reported on Tuesday. The trial, run by the state atmospheric sciences institute, used aircraft to release salt-based particles into monsoon clouds on 48 occasions across two monsoon seasons. Lead researcher Dr. Arvind Kulkarni cautioned that the effect, while statistically detectable, is smaller than many farmers had hoped for and is not large enough to end drought risk on its own. The trial cost 22 crore rupees, and the institute estimates that scaling the programme across the state would cost about 140 crore rupees per season. The institute has recommended a further three-year study focused on the most drought-prone districts before any statewide rollout, and has published its full dataset for other research groups to verify the findings.

Invoice financing volumes among the association's 2,400 member firms rose 42 percent in the first half of the year, while new term loans from banks fell 19 percent over the same period. Under invoice financing, a firm sells its outstanding invoices to a finance company at a small discount, receiving cash within days instead of waiting the typical 60 to 90 days for customers to pay. Association secretary Rahul Bhide said the shift reflects both slower bank approvals and longer payment delays from large corporate buyers, which now average 74 days, up from 61 days two years ago. Finance companies typically charge between 1.5 and 3 percent per month, making the service costlier than a bank loan but faster to obtain. Economists warn that heavy reliance on invoice financing can squeeze already thin margins, and the association has asked the state government to enforce a 45-day payment cap for government contracts.

A district schools athletics programme launched three years ago has produced its first three national-level qualifiers, officials announced after the state championships on Sunday. Sprinter Asha Kamble, 16, won the under-18 100 metres in 12.41 seconds, while middle-distance runners Vikram Shinde and Farhan Qureshi qualified in the 800 metres and 1500 metres respectively. The programme gives 40 selected students free coaching, two meals a day, and travel support, at an annual cost of 55 lakh rupees shared between the district sports office and a corporate sponsor. Coach Suresh Rane said the results came from consistent year-round training rather than any single innovation, noting that the athletes train six days a week on a cinder track that becomes unusable during heavy rain. The three qualifiers will travel to the national junior championships next month, and the sports office says it will add a residential hostel for out-of-town athletes if the district's funding application succeeds.

Migratory birds have returned to the Kasarde wetland in large numbers for the first time in over a decade, following a four-year restoration project, the forest department reported this week. The project removed invasive water hyacinth from 60 hectares, rebuilt two breached embankments, and diverted treated water from a nearby sewage plant to maintain water levels through the dry season. Local fishing cooperatives, which initially opposed restrictions, now report that fish catches in adjoining channels have recovered, and the cooperatives run the visitor centre that opened last year. Ecologist Dr. Nandini Pawar said the return of bar-headed geese, which migrate over the Himalayas, indicates the wetland once again offers safe roosting conditions. The department plans a bird-ringing study next winter to track where the visitors breed, and has proposed protecting two smaller marshes nearby that serve as overflow feeding grounds.

The state education department announced on Thursday that its free coaching scheme for national competitive examinations will expand from 12 to 30 centres, admitting 4,500 students this year. The scheme offers ten months of coaching, printed study material, and a monthly stipend of 1,500 rupees to students from families earning less than 3 lakh rupees per year. Last year, 38 percent of the scheme's 1,800 students cleared the first stage of at least one national examination, compared with a statewide average of about 9 percent among all candidates. Education minister S. D. Patil said centres will be placed in districts with the fewest private coaching institutes, selected using enrollment data from the past five years. The department says 60 percent of instructors will be permanent hires this year, and it will publish centre-wise results annually so that underperforming centres can be restructured.

The municipal council voted 41 to 19 on Tuesday night to approve new safety rules for establishments employing night-shift workers, ending a debate that stretched across five sessions. Under the rules, workplaces with more than 20 night-shift employees must provide secure transport home, install panic buttons in restrooms and parking areas, and maintain a register of cab drivers verified by the police. The rules were first proposed three years ago after a survey by a workers' welfare group found that 62 percent of night-shift employees, most of them women in the retail and health-care sectors, felt unsafe commuting after 10 pm. Business associations argued the transport requirement would be unaffordable for small firms, and the final text exempts workplaces with fewer than 20 night staff while offering a two-year tax rebate to those that comply early. Opposition councillors criticised the exemption as a loophole, but the mayor said a phased approach was the only version that could pass.

A weavers' cooperative in the district has signed its first export contract, agreeing to supply 40,000 metres of handloom cotton fabric to a European clothing brand over the next year, the cooperative announced on Saturday. The cooperative, which was formed eight years ago and nearly closed during the pandemic, credits the turnaround to a design consultant hired with a state handloom board grant, who helped members adapt traditional patterns to the brand's specifications. Export quality standards required the cooperative to replace 35 ageing looms and install a small testing lab to check fabric strength and colour fastness, investments totalling 48 lakh rupees financed through a cooperative bank loan. The brand's representative visited twice during negotiations and conducted a social-compliance audit covering working hours and child-labour rules, which the cooperative passed. The cooperative is now negotiating with two more foreign buyers and plans to train 60 younger weavers this year to replace retiring members.

The Prabhat Theatre, a single-screen cinema that closed eleven years ago, reopened on Sunday as a community arts centre after a three-year restoration funded by public donations and a heritage grant. Restoration cost 6.8 crore rupees, of which 2.5 crore came from more than 4,000 small donors through a crowdfunding campaign, with the remainder from the state heritage department. Architects retained the 1954 facade, the original projection room and the balcony's cast-iron railings, while replacing the roof, wiring and seating. The centre will be run by a non-profit trust, which expects ticket sales and café income to cover about 70 percent of operating costs, with the rest from the heritage department's annual maintenance grant. Film historian Anand Ksheersagar, who advised the project, said the theatre is one of only nine art-deco cinemas surviving in the region.
